extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary authors, and educated readers of 18th‑century criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for composing episodes and digressions in epic or narrative poetry: keep episodes relevant to the main action, place them appropriately, preserve character and tone, render philosophical or technical matter with concision and perspicuity, and aim for natural but not obvious invention. Emphasis on moral suitability and tasteful integration of source material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode relevance to principal action
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Accounts which Raphael gives of the Battel of Angels, and the Creation of the World, have in them those Qualifications which the Criticks judge requisite to an Episode. They are nearly related to the principal Action, and have a just Connexion with the Fable.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make episodes closely connected to the main plot/fable — they should feel like a natural extension of the principal action rather than an irrelevant diversion. Use episodes to illuminate or advance the central narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate placement and reservation of episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: "As our Author knew this Subject could not but be agreeable to his Reader, he would not throw it into the Relation of the six days Works, but reserved it for a distinct Episode, that he might have an opportunity of expatiating upon it more at large.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place large or attractive digressions where they can be properly expanded (as distinct episodes) rather than inserting them awkwardly into other sections; reserve material to give it suitable scope and emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness combined with novelty (not obvious)
rubrics_metrics.description: "These and the like wonderful Incidents in this Part of the Work, have in them all the Beauties of Novelty, at the same time that they have all the Graces of Nature... tho they are natural, they are not obvious, which is the true Character of all fine Writing.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for inventions and images that feel organic to the subject (natural) but are not clichéd or predictable (not obvious). Strive for originality that seems to arise inevitably from the matter at hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and perspicuity in explaining technical or philosophical matter
rubrics_metrics.description: "The chief Points in the Ptolemaick and Copernican Hypothesis are described with great Conciseness and Perspicuity, and at the same time dressed in very pleasing and poetical Images.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When summarizing complex theories or technical ideas in verse or narration, be concise and clear, yet embellish with tasteful poetic imagery so the matter is both intelligible and pleasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid granting authoritative sanction to controversial systems via poetic authority
rubrics_metrics.description: "It would have been highly absurd to have given the Sanction of an Archangel to any particular System of Philosophy.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about putting contested doctrines into the mouths of authoritative or supernatural speakers; avoid implying the poet/narrator endorses a specific philosophical system when using elevated or divine voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve appropriate character voices and tonal consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Poet has wonderfully preserved the Character of Majesty and Condescension in the Creator, and at the same time that of Humility and Adoration in the Creature...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain distinct, consistent characterizations and tones in dialogue and narration (e.g., majesty for divine figures, humility for created beings). Voice and manner should suit each role and remain steady throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict love and passion with chastity and purity while retaining transport
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tho this Part of the Poem is work'd up with great Warmth and Spirit, the Love which is described in it is every way suitable to a State of Innocence... The Sentiments are chaste, but not cold; and convey to the Mind Ideas of the most transporting Passion, and of the greatest Purity.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render erotic or amorous feeling so that it is emotionally powerful yet morally decorous when the subject demands it: intense feeling without indecency; avoid language or images offensive to religion or good manners in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid sensory detail and strong judgment in description
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of Adam's first sensations and landscape: "As new waked from soundest Sleep, Soft on the flowry Herb I found me laid... With Fragrance, and with Joy my Heart o'erflow'd.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ concrete sensory imagery (sight, smell, sound, touch) with confident, judicious selection to stimulate reader attention and evoke wonder. Strong, well-judged description raises reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate source/sacred material respectfully with original imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Poet has interwoven every thing which is delivered upon this Subject in Holy Writ with so many beautiful Imaginations of his own...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting or expanding material drawn from scripture, history, or other authoritative sources, blend faithful elements of the source with tasteful invention — respect the original while contributing imaginative elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use admonition and foreshadowing artfully to prepare the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: "These Sentiments of Love... gave the Angel such an Insight into Humane Nature, that he seems apprehensive of the Evils which might befall the Species... He therefore fortifies him against it by timely Admonitions; which very artfully prepare the Mind of the Reader for the Occurrences of the next Book...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy gentle rebuke, warnings, or foreshadowing within dialogue or narrative to signal and prepare readers for forthcoming developments; such devices should feel natural to characters and motive, not contrived.
